PAGE	126
P	Stonetop sits on the easternmost edge of the <b>Flats</b>, a rolling tallgrass prairie that stretches all the way to the <b>Huffel Peaks</b> (page 236), the <b>Foothills</b> (page 144) and the <b>Steplands</b> (page 372).

HR

B	Mountains looming on the far horizon

B	Birds of prey, or carrion eaters, floating high above
B	Clouds, always in motion: high and wispy, or big and fluffy, or massive and dark like an anvil ready to drop

B	Green and yellow stems topped with a riot of flowers, rippling and bobbing in the wind
B	The itch and scratch of nettles, thistle, and stiff sandpaper stalks
B	Constant noise: birdsong, insect-buzz, rustling grass
B	Relentless sun, unbroken by shade
B	A wall of rain, rolling towards you The prairie is dotted with small hills, outcrops, and the occasional copse of trees huddled against the ceaseless wind. Winding streams cut through the soil. But mostly?
P	Just mile after mile after mile of grass.

B	The cold, wet, exhausting trudge through waist-high drifts
B	The squeak of snow underfoot on a bitterly cold day
PAGE	127
H2	The Gwead
HR
P	Villagers call the Flats-grasses <b>the Gwead</b> ("the Weave" or "the Weaving"). It's a bewildering array of species. Some are short and wispy, others thick and taller than a tall man. They bloom in a myriad of shapes and colors, and sport every manner of prickle, thorn, and seedpod.
P	The Gwead will not be tamed. Burn the grasses, plow the soil, tear things up by their roots—it doesn't matter. The Gwead always come back, thicker and hardier than before. And sometimes, it seems, the grasslands take their revenge.
Q	When was the last time anyone tried to plant crops beyond the Old Wall?
Q	What uncanny fate befell them?
P	Why can crops be managed within the <b>Old</b> <b>Wall</b> (page 12), but not beyond? That's for you to decide. Maybe…
E	magic tied to the <b>Stone</b> (page 12) makes the land more pliable, easier to tame;
E	something buried beneath the Old Wall keeps the Gwead at bay;
E	something about the soil keeps the Gwead from taking root; or
E	whoever built the ruins on which Stonetop was founded, they made a pact with the spirits of the Gwead.
H2	Questions
HR
Q	Who among you has ventured deep into the Flats? What did you see there that no one quite believes?
Q	Aside from sticking to the roads, what keeps the pack drakes at bay?
Q	Which of you has seen a prairie fire up close and personal?
Q	What flower, root, seed, or stem that can be found on the Flats is particularly useful? How so? Why is it so hard to harvest?

H2	Dangers
HR
H3	Hazards
B	Nasty turn in the weather: lashing wind, bitter cold, blistering heat, sleet/ hail/rain/snow; lightning
B	Lack of shelter, water, or wood for a long-burning fire (try dried aurochs dung, if you can find it)
B	Hidden holes/burrows, twisting an ankle or worse
B	Getting lost (lack of landmarks, tall grass and rolling terrain, hard to keep to a straight line)
HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Prairie fire
P	The Gwead is prone to burning, sparked by lightning, an errant flame, or (if you believe the tales) Hillfolk intentionally setting the Flats ablaze. Early spring, late summer, and early autumn are particularly prone, especially after a few weeks without rain.
P	<b>Instinct</b> to run unchecked across the land
P	• Start with just a few crackling flames, a column of smoke
P	• Grow implacably, creeping outward
P	• Smother the landscape in choking smoke (debilities)
P	• Hit them with a wave of heat (d4 damage)
P	• Linger and burn for minutes or hours (d6 damage, messy)
P	• Tear a crimson line, faster than you can sprint, bonfire-hot (d10 damage, ignores armor, messy)
P	• Run out of fuel, or get smothered by rain
P	<b>Something interesting</b>: To really spread and burn hot, a prairie fire needs years of built-up fuel, dry conditions, and steady wind; even then, it can only burn at its hottest for a short period of time.
P	<b>Something useful</b>: Seek the Makers' Roads, or barren ground, or low-lying patches that still hold some moisture. Failing that, seek patches of grass that burned in the past year. Worst case: seek a narrow point in the fire-head and run through it, into the ash-fields behind.
P	Also: pray.

H3	Aurochs
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>ornery</i>, <i>powerful</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 14, <b>Armor</b> 2 (thick hide, tough)
P	<b>Damage</b> gore d8+5 (<i>close</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>messy</i>,
P	1 piercing), kick/trample d8+3 (<i>hand</i>,
P	<i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to spook or to get angry, in equal measure
P	• Send an attacker flying
P	• Stampede (<i>area</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>messy</i>)
P	• Wheel suddenly, with surprising grace and speed
P	• Keep going past when it should be dead or dying
P	Big, powerful, wild cattle with horns longer than your arm and thicker than your hand can grip around. Even the does have big horns, and aren't shy about using them.
P	They winter in the Steplands, in small bands of 3-5 adults. In spring, though, they come down to the Flats, form up into herds of 30 or more, and graze and graze and graze. They'll break up into smaller bands by midsummer, then head back into the hills before first snow.
P	The Hillfolk hunt them, riding at the flanks of a herd and picking off one or two with arrows, keeping their damned distance. You do not want to get too close to one of these things, especially not after you wound it.
P	A full-grown aurochs carcass (<i>immobile</i>), properly butchered and transported back to town, counts as 1 Surplus. A ◇◇ pair of aurochs horns is Value 1.

H3	Bandit
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>devious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 6; <b>Armor</b> up to 2 (hides, shields)
P	<b>Damage</b> spears d8 (<i>close</i>, <i>thrown</i>) or slings d6 (<i>near</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to survive at the expense of others
P	• Prepare a deception, to lure travelers from the roads
P	• Spring an ambush when their prey takes the bait
P	• Take captives or slit throats, so that no one escapes to tell tales
P	• Flee into the grass if things go south
P	The magic of the Roads and the open terrain make a life of banditry far from easy, but somehow, they crop up every few years.
P	Might be Hillfolk, disgraced or desperate, but more often than not, they're scoundrels who'd rather bleed their fellows than scrape by up in Gordin's Delve.

P	Most bandit gangs struggle to find victims or shelter or both, and quickly die out or disband. The clever ones last a few seasons, but eventually folk catch wise and grow wary, and the bandits' schemes start to fail.
P	But every generation or so, a leader crops up who's cagey enough to turn a gang of bandits into a serious threat.

H3	Beznpol
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>fierce</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 12; <b>Armor</b> 3 <b>Damage</b> burrowing talons d10 (<i>hand</i>), needle teeth d8 (<i>hand</i>, <i>messy</i>, 3 piercing)
P	<b>Special Qualities</b> acid-proof
P	<b>Instinct</b> to constantly search for food
P	• Dig up serious quantities of soil
P	• Bound out of the grass and onto prey
P	• Spray a stupefying musk (<i>reach</i>, <i>area</i>, debilities)
P	• Curl up into a ball of hard, jagged scales (4 armor)
P	Great big armored mustelids, like a cross between a stoat, a badger, and a pangolin, but like 6 feet long not counting the tail.
P	They roam the Flats digging up burrows of just about anything, but they especially love to stir up a <b>hlomren</b> (page 134) nest and chomp chomp chomp. They're far from the top of the food chain, though. If startled, they'll spray musk and attempt to flee. If cornered, they'll curl up and hope the attacker grows bored.
P	A skilled tanner can turn a pair of hides into a magnificent ◇◇ beznpol scale coat (2 armor, <i>warm</i>, protects against acid, Value 3). Hillfolk champions are known to wear them.

H3	Frythanc
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>terrifying</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 0 <b>Damage</b> swooping talons d10+2 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>grabby</i>), beak d10 (<i>reach</i>, disadvantage)
P	<b>Special Qualities</b> incredible eyesight, terrible hearing <b>Instinct</b> to wait for the right moment
P	• Soar on thermals, thousands of feet up
P	• Swoop down like a thunderbolt, snatching up prey
P	• Drag prey up to 30 or 40 feet with slow, mighty flaps—then drop them
P	Great scaly birds, wings like 40 feet across, sky blue and white feathers on their undersides to hide in the sky. They're said to roost in the Huffel Peaks but hunt the Flats, snatching up the unwary—man, woman, deer, horse—and dropping them to the ground. The drop usually kills or cripples its prey, and then it alights to dine at its leisure.
P	They are, thank Tor, very rare, with only one mated pair hunting the Flats at a time.
P	On the other side of the Huffel Peaks, though… who knows?

H3	Hlomren
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>tiny</i>, <i>organized</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 1; <b>Armor</b> 3 (carapace, size)
P	<b>Damage</b> acid-dripping mandibles d6-2 (<i>hand</i>, <i>messy</i>, 3 piercing), acid glob d6-2 (<i>reach</i>, <i>messy</i>, <i>reload</i>, 1 piercing)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to protect the colony
P	• Burrow into/out of/through loose soil
P	• Swarm over a threat
P	• Burst with acid when killed, d4 damage (<i>close</i>, <i>area</i>)
P	These red-shelled insects look like a cross between an ant and a beetle, but the size of a small cat. They form colonies a few-hundred large, typically on higher ground. A colony will harvest all the dead grass in a few miles, hibernate through winter, and then relocate in spring to a part of the Flats that hasn't burned or been harvested in a few years. They mostly ignore people and other large animals, but they'll swarm if threatened.

P	• Drag it beneath the soil, to be crushed and supped on at leisure
P	Great big beetles that live out beneath the Flats, preying on large game like horses and aurochs. The Hillfolk know what signs to watch for, but they rarely tell outsiders. What better way to keep the Flats free of fools?

P	• Bite down and pull in one direction while a packmate pulls in the other (+<i>messy</i>)
P	Sneaky little dog-sized critters that prowl the Flats. Hunt in packs ranging from six to a couple dozen. Just the worst.

H3	Shellback drake
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>hardy</i>, <i>patient</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 3 (carapace, scales)
P	<b>Damage</b> snapping, bone-crushing bite d10 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing)
P	<b>Special Qualities</b> nearly blind, senses vibrations <b>Instinct</b> to lash out at "food" in range
P	• Burrow into soil
P	• Wait for prey half-buried
P	• Withdraw into its shell (Armor 5)
P	Like a snapping turtle, but 6 feet long and 400 pounds, with big, badger-like claws.
P	Way faster than you think. It'll dig itself under a layer of soil, and wait long enough for the gwead to start growing over it. Then, when something comes near? SNAP!
P	An intact shell is worth quite a bit (<i>immobile</i>, Value 2). But good luck killing one without cracking the shell.

H3	Thunder drake
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 20; <b>Armor</b> 3 (scales, crest)
P	<b>Damage</b> gore, trample, swat d10+3 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing)
P	<b>Special Qualities</b> lightning-proof, hard of hearing
P	<b>Instinct</b> to protect its turf
P	• Bellow (<i>near</i>, <i>area</i>, <i>loud</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>reload</i>)
P	• Burrow and gnaw through rock
P	• Sometimes: belch forth a bolt of lightning, d10+3 damage (<i>near</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>loud</i>, ignores armor)
P	Sometimes, out on the Flats, you'll see what looks to be small hills in the distance.
P	I advise you to steer clear. They probably aren't hills, really, but huge piles of dirt that a thunder drake has moved as it digs. And hoo boy, you do not want to stumble into one of them on their home turf.
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> Thunder drakes eat mostly grass and shrubs, but they have a taste for certain ores. They spend their time grazing, sleeping, and digging up rocks.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> They particularly savor the taste of copper, and relish <b>aetherium</b> (page 404). If they find a source of it, they'll chew it right up and spend the next few days belching lightning bolts.
P	When you <b><i>are near a thunder drake when</i></b> <b><i>it bellows</i></b>, roll +CON: <b>on a 10+</b>, pick 1; <b>on</b> <b>a 7-9,</b> pick 2; <b>on a 6-</b>, all 3.
B	Drop what you're holding and cover your ears
B	Stagger back a few steps
B	You're deafened and disoriented for a few moments
ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Wild horse
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>swift</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 10; <b>Armor</b> 0 <b>Damage</b> trample d6+3 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to panic
P	• Sniff trouble on the wind
P	• Run free!
P	• Vault over an obstacle
P	They roam the flats, in herds ranging in size from a half-dozen to a couple dozen.
P	The larger herds will give rise to a <b>ceffylwraig</b> (page 368).
